newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index rallies six pct on New Year's Day.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index rallies six pct on New Year's Day.

text.p: Share prices at Bombay bourses recorded huge gains on Wednesday in a session that saw hectic volatility sparked by improved market sentiment, traders said.
"It's mainly a speculative bull run helped by a little bit of short-covering," said chief dealer Sanjeev Sanghvi at foreign brokerage James Capel B&K.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) top index leapt 184.84 points to 3,270.04, an intra-day high over its previous close.
Government officials on Tuesday said the government would announce a series of policy measures this month to boost industrial growth and sagging markets.

"The government is likely to announce the decisions early January," H.K. Dua, information advisor to the prime minister, told reporters at the end of a five-hour meeting between industrialists and the Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
Market participants said the good news came at a time of depressed sentiment and widespread concern about the slowdown in the economy.

"Basically, the government has said it will take a broader look at the economy. This has given optimism for operators to pick up stocks," said institutional dealer, Ashish Wakankar at broking firm Sundar Iyer.
Some dealers said second tier stocks also recorded sharp gains indicating strength in the rally. "There is a flare-up in across-the board counters," Sundar Iyer's Wakankar said.

ICICI rose 5.25 rupees to 64.0 while SCICI fell 1.0 to 25.25. On Tuesday, the two boards approved a proposal to merge SCICI with ICICI. The swap ratio will be two shares of ICICI for every five of SCICI, effective from April 1, 1996.
ACC jumped 129.70 rupees to 1,320.0, SBI 20.0 to 246.50, TISCO 18.50 to 182.25, ITC 37.0 to 343.0, L&T 14.25 to 233.0, Reliance 14.75 to 218.0 and TELCO 25.0 362.0
